stem: Which kind of sampling lets you apply statistical tests and generalise your results to the whole population?
explanation: Probability sampling allows statistical tests and generalisation to the whole population, while non-probability sampling (convenience, volunteer panels) does not give such robust generalisation.
source: CSC 531 Lecture 4 (2025), slides 'Identifying Participants'; HCI 2021-22 past question 4(d)(ii)

stem: Which type of interview is most appropriate when the goals of the study are clear and well understood?
explanation: Structured interviews ask the same pre-determined questions of each user and are most appropriate when goals are clear; unstructured interviews are open-ended and exploratory.
source: CSC 531 Lecture 4 (2025), slides 'Data Gathering Techniques' and 'Interview'

options.text: The time users take to complete a task
The number of outliers in a scatter diagram
The sample size needed for a finite population
The internal consistency, or reliability, of a set of survey items

explanation: Cronbach's alpha measures internal consistency on a 0 to 1 scale; higher values mean the items agree and probably measure the same characteristic.

stem: An experiment tests whether the input device (mouse or trackpad) affects how long users take to complete a task. What is the task completion time?

options.text: A level of the independent variable

explanation: Dependent variables are what we measure, such as completion time or number of errors; the input device is the independent variable.
source: CSC 531 Lecture 5 (2025), slide 'Inferential Analysis'; CSC 531 2023/24 past question 3(b)

stem: People who take part in a pilot study are typically also involved in the main study.
explanation: A pilot study is a small trial of the main study, and the people involved in it are typically not involved in the main study.
source: CSC 531 Lecture 4 (2025), slide 'Pilot Studies'; HCI 2020-21 past question 3(b)

stem: A scatter diagram is useful for identifying outliers in the data easily.
explanation: Scatter diagrams make outliers easy to see; outliers can distort a representation but may also be of interest.
source: CSC 531 Lecture 5 (2025), slide 'Graphical Representation of Data'; CSC 531 2023/24 past question 5(a)

stem: Which of these are types of triangulation named in the lecture? Select all that apply.
explanation: The four types are methodological (combining techniques), data (different sources, times and places), investigator (different researchers) and theories (different frameworks).

stem: Which are ways of observing users indirectly? Select all that apply.

options.text: Watching users think aloud in a usability lab

explanation: Indirect observation uses diaries, interaction logs and web analytics; watching users in the field or in a usability lab is direct observation.
source: CSC 531 Lectures 2-3 (2024), slides 'Observation'; HCI 2021-22 past question 4(d)(iv)

stem: Three of these are probability sampling methods. Which is the odd one out?

options.text: Selecting every nth person on the list

explanation: Random generators, every nth person and stratified sampling are probability methods; volunteer panels rely on people willing to take part, so they are non-probability.

stem: Three of these are techniques for simple qualitative analysis. Which is the odd one out?
explanation: Affinity diagrams, thematic analysis and identifying recurring themes are qualitative; percentages are simple quantitative statistics, best used with at least 10 users.
source: CSC 531 Lecture 5 (2025), slides 'Simple Qualitative Analysis' and 'Simple Statistics Analysis'; CSC 531 2023/24 past question 2(b)(a)
